title: Deterministic Vortex Generation from Coupled Trapped Polariton Condensate Triad
authors: X. Qin, N. Pitanios, S. Dam, S. Betzold, S. Höfling, S. V. Koniakhin, P. G. Savvidis
abstract: We present the deterministic generation and all-optical switching of ternary topologically distinct vortex states in a triad of trapped exciton-polariton condensates with direct state readout from momentum-space emission distribution. Tuning the non-resonant pump power controls the sign of the dissipative coupling, selecting between a ferromagnetic in-phase state and two frustrated states with global phase winding. The zero-winding ferromagnetic state has unstructured far-field emission at low momenta and forms vortex-antivortex arrays at the Dirac points, reflecting the C_3v global symmetry. The two frustrated states of +-2pi winding can be activated on-demand by a control beam and produce different triangular emission patterns selectively localized at the K or K' points. Although all three states share identical real-space emission distributions, their momentum-space photoluminescence profiles distinguish them unambiguously, revealing the chirality without the need for interferometry. This enables on-demand orbital angular momentum control using a pump independent of resonant phase or OAM imprinting, establishing condensate triads as a compact platform for reconfigurable chiral light generation operating on a ternary logic basis.
summary: The research demonstrates how a triad of trapped exciton-polariton condensates can deterministically generate and switch between three distinct topological vortex states. By tuning the pump power and using a control beam, the system achieves on-demand control over the global phase winding, which is unambiguously read out via momentum-space light emission. This establishes the condensate triad as a powerful, compact platform for reconfigurable chiral light sources.
main_problem: The paper addresses the deterministic generation and all-optical switching of topologically distinct vortex states in a triad of trapped exciton-polariton condensates.
main_result: The system establishes the condensate triad as a compact platform for reconfigurable chiral light generation, enabling on-demand orbital angular momentum control using a ternary logic basis.
method: The study combines experimental measurements of momentum-space photoluminescence (PL) with theoretical modeling using coupled Stuart-Landau and Gross-Pitaevskii equations.
model_or_system: The physical system is a triad of trapped exciton-polariton condensates in a microcavity. The dynamics are modeled by coupled equations incorporating hopping/Josephson coupling and dissipative terms, reflecting the $C_{3v}$ symmetry.
key_observables: Momentum-space photoluminescence profiles, quantized phase winding ($\pm 2\pi$), and the ability to distinguish topological states without interferometry.
important_parameters: Non-resonant pump power (controls coupling sign), control beam intensity, and the sign of the dissipative coupling ($D$).
main_assumptions: The system can be effectively described by the coupled Stuart-Landau or Gross-Pitaevskii mean-field equations, and the control beam can deterministically break symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup, spatial excitation patterns, and crucial momentum-space PL profiles comparing zero-winding (ferromagnetic) states against $\pm 2\pi$ winding states, demonstrating the unique signatures in K and K' points.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the basic coupled model (dyad/triad) to demonstrating the control over phase winding via pump tuning, culminating in the unique characterization of chirality and OAM control using momentum-space imaging.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it uses polariton condensates—a platform bridging quantum optics and condensed matter—to demonstrate robust, deterministic control over topological quantum numbers (OAM/chirality) in a solid-state system.
